title: When it is recited, listen
hook: when the Qur'an is recited, listen and be silent (7:204–205)

segments.voice: Yesterday: al-asma' al-husna, call Him by His names. Your line was the names are for calling. Today, the last verses of surah seven, and an instruction about your ears.
screen: `AL-ASMA' AL-HUSNA — THE NAMES ARE FOR CALLING.`

segments.voice: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once asked a companion, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, to recite the Qur'an to him. Ibn Mas'ud was surprised: recite it to you, when it was revealed to you? The Prophet said he loved to hear it from someone else. So Ibn Mas'ud began surah four, the Women. When he reached a verse about the Day when each community brings a witness, the Prophet said, enough. Ibn Mas'ud looked up and saw his eyes full of tears. The one who brought the Qur'an, listening to it, in silence.
screen: `RECITE IT TO ME.` → `I LOVE TO HEAR IT FROM ANOTHER.` → `HIS EYES FULL OF TEARS.`

segments.voice: Surah seven ends with three verses that begin with that kind of listening. Verse two-oh-four, in Pickthall's words: “And when the Qur'an is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that ye may obtain mercy.” Two Arabic verbs. Istami'u: listen closely, lean in with your hearing. Ansitu: be silent, the silence of someone paying attention, not merely not talking. In Mecca, surah forty-one reports, some opponents told each other to make noise whenever the Qur'an was recited, to drown it out. This verse asks for the opposite. Jurists also debated what it means in congregational prayer. Hanafi scholars say the one praying behind an imam should stay silent while he recites, citing this verse. Shafi'i scholars hold that each person still recites al-Fatiha quietly, citing a hadith. Both take the verse seriously; they differ on how it applies. Verse two-oh-five continues: remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and with awe, below the voice, morning and evening, and don't be among the heedless. And the last verse, two-oh-six, says those near your Lord are not too proud to worship Him; they glorify Him and prostrate to Him. In the order of the mushaf, it's the first of the verses at which reciters and listeners traditionally bow down in prostration. So al-A'raf ends here: ears open, voice low, forehead on the ground.
screen: `ISTAMI'U — LISTEN CLOSELY.` · `ANSITU — ATTENTIVE SILENCE.` · `BEHIND THE IMAM: THEY DIFFER.` · `THE FIRST PROSTRATION VERSE.` · then, large: `GIVE EAR TO IT AND PAY HEED.`

segments.voice: Play a short recitation at a low volume, any reciter, any surah, or sit in silence and recall one you've heard, or simply listen to the room. Don't follow along on a screen or try to translate; just listen, the way the Prophet listened to Ibn Mas'ud, still and open, letting the sound arrive.
Ansitu, be silent, attentively. Surah seven, verse two-oh-four: when the Qur'an is recited, listen closely and be silent, that you may receive mercy. Today's word.
Your line: listen, be still. And with that, surah seven, the Heights, is finished. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims listen to Qur'an recitation in silence, at home, in the mosque and on the radio; at 7:206, the first prostration verse in the mushaf, reciters and listeners traditionally make a prostration of recitation.

fork.setup: you're Ibn Mas'ud, reciting to the Prophet. he says, enough. you look up. what do you see?
options: his eyes are full of tears.
fork.reveal: his eyes were overflowing with tears at the verse about the witness for each community (4:41).

trapdoor: what you thought: be quiet when someone reads the Qur'an.
what it means: listen closely and keep an attentive silence, so mercy can reach you, as the Prophet himself listened.
what a scholar hears: insat is attentive silence, not mere quiet; Hanafi and Shafi'i jurists apply 7:204 differently to recitation behind the imam.
recall: the covenant, a firmly bound pledge

chat.says: Why do people go so quiet when the Qur'an is being recited?
options: The Qur'an (7:204) says: when it's recited, listen closely and stay quiet, so you may receive mercy.
Because talking during recitation breaks a person's wudu, so they must wash again.
Because only the reciter is allowed to understand it, so everyone else just waits.
chat.meaning: When the Qur'an is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that ye may obtain mercy (7:204): istami'u, listen closely; ansitu, attentive silence.

mushaf.meaning: the Qur'an as a written, bound copy

Hanafi.meaning: one of the Sunni schools of law

Shafi'i.meaning: another of the Sunni schools of law

sources.quoted: And when the Qur'an is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that ye may obtain mercy.
